Alex: Customer-ACME sent a short security questionnaire asking about log redaction, who can access logs, and retention (SOC2-related). Can someone confirm our posture so I can send a bulleted answer?
Maria: Thanks — can you paste the exact questions or attach the form?
Alex: Pasted below (redacted):
> 1) What PII is logged? 2) How is PII redacted? 3) Who has access to logs? 4) Encryption in transit/rest? 5) Subprocessors storing logs?
Sam: Quick answers:
- We do NOT log full PII by default (we hash/store ids).
- Redaction happens in the shipper pipeline (log-shipper -> redact stage) with patterns + field allowlist.
- Access: SRE + SecEng groups via Okta, mfa enforced. All access audited.
Jules: Add retention details: prod app logs retained 90 days, audit/security logs retained 365 days. Dev/staging logs 7 days.
Sam: Example redact config (shipper):
```
{ "stages": [ {"type":"redact","patterns":["email","credit_card","ssn"],"replace_with":"[REDACTED]"} ] }
```
Maria: For subprocessors: we forward metrics/logs to Datadog and store aggregates in BigQuery (both covered by DPA). Will that be ok to state?
Jules: Yes, mention Datadog + GCP BigQuery as subprocessors; note they have SOC2/ISO attestations. Also call out KMS for at-rest key management.
Alex: Perfect. I'll draft the response. Can someone +1 the final blurb before I send to AE? @Maria @Jules
Maria: +1
Jules: +1 :thumbsup:
sec-bot: NOTE: create a ticket in SEC-OPS to capture the customer response for audit trail.
Alex: Filed SEC-OPS-3421. Thanks everyone :tada:
